clue.text: Act of getting professional treatment taking fellows time

parts.note: PRO is the short form of professional
a cure is a course of medical treatment
fellows are men

explanation.surface: A professional treatment session that takes up the doctors' time.
explanation.definitionFit: Procuring something is obtaining it, so the noun names the business of acquiring goods or supplies.

clue.text: Bring up the thing that may be brought up

definitions.text: the thing that may be brought up

explanation.surface: Raising a child, or something else that gets raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense rests on the idiom 'bring up the rear', to come last in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a child is to raise it; the back end of a procession is the part someone brings up in the idiom.

clue.text: Clever copper starts to teach experts

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A smart policeman begins teaching specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer; it is the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute in its informal sense means shrewd or sharp-witted, as in a cute move.

clue.text: Unscrupulous schemes to make money from game

explanation.surface: Dishonest money-making schemes run off the back of a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is played with a ball against the walls of a court, an older relative of squash.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a fraudulent scheme for profit, and the plural also names a court sport played with strung bats.

clue.text: Mum'll walk

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
the contraction of will or shall is written LL after an apostrophe

explanation.surface: Mother is going to go for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The single printed word splits at its apostrophe into two pieces, mother and the shortened 'will'; 'walk' at the end is the definition, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is a sheltered promenade or public walk, as with The Mall in London.

clue.text: Very much 'pa' rather than 'papa'?

explanation.surface: A question about baby talk for father, short or doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang meaning 'very much so'. The second reading is playful: 'pa' is exactly half of 'papa', so the setter teases with the phrase that sounds like a denial.
explanation.definitionFit: The British exclamation is an emphatic yes, meaning extremely; the second sense plays on the two-letter word being half the four-letter one.

clue.text: I run home

parts.note: read as a speaker describing their job: someone who manages a household's domestic affairs

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of sprinting back to base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like sprinting; here it means manage, as in running a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic employee who manages the running of a house would say they run the home.

clue.text: Almost the last minute — leapt in a frenzy

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild disorder, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone jumps about wildly at the eleventh hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Penultimate means next to final, one before the end of a series.

clue.text: Trunk with nothing left inside to be put outside

indicators.note: inside places the letters for nothing and left within those for to be

parts.note: to be, the infinitive, gives BE
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A suitcase emptied of its contents is to be left out on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put outside' says BE goes around the inner letters O and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A bole is the main stem of a tree, a botanical word for its trunk.

clue.text: President — coherent in speech or bitty?

parts.note: someone articulate speaks clearly and fluently

explanation.surface: A question of whether the head of state talks sense or rambles in fragments.
explanation.definitionFit: Particulate matter consists of separate tiny particles, so it is made up of little bits.

clue.text: Some see Saul as a significant "old testament" character

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people regard King Saul as a key Bible figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition began with 'as', a link word that cannot stand in for a name; the definition is the phrase after it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the elder twin of Jacob who sold his birthright for a meal of stew is a major figure.

clue.text: Fine sloppy depot for threat to health?

indicators.note: sloppy means careless and untidy, so the letters of the word fine are jumbled

parts.note: a depot is a bus or railway station

explanation.surface: A fine for a badly kept depot that puts health at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm of vermin or parasites in a building endangers the health of those living there, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Appearance of noble lady, nice one coming out

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
Ena is a woman's name, a crossword stalwart

indicators.note: coming out removes a letter from the word nice

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The looks of an aristocratic woman, a pleasant one, making her debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noble lady' looks like one person; it is two pieces, a nobleman then a woman's name. 'coming out' leaves NCE from NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Countenance is a literary word for the face or expression, a person's outward look.

clue.text: Old artefact in hotel given special display

indicators.note: a special display rearranges the letters of the words in hotel into a fresh layout

explanation.surface: An antique put on show in a hotel lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a Stone Age tool or object from the New Stone Age, so an ancient relic.

clue.text: Tend to hide love, being a cruel king

indicators.note: to hide means the first piece wraps around the second and conceals it

parts.note: to herd animals is to look after them
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A tyrant who tends to conceal any affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is the biblical ruler of Judaea who ordered the massacre of the infants.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruler of Judaea in the Gospels is remembered as a byword for tyranny after the slaughter of the innocents.

clue.text: Piece of material left in carton

indicators.note: in places the letter for left within the word for carton

parts.note: a carton is a packet, as of cigarettes

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric is found left inside a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A placket is a slit or opening in a garment, often with an overlapping strip of fabric.

clue.text: Longed to get some sleep in Edinburgh

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for a night's rest in the Scottish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Longed to get' as the definition; 'to get' is the link, since a past tense verb alone stands in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to yearn or ache for something absent.

clue.text: Not a whole letter, just a line

definitions.text: Not a whole letter, just a line

parts.words: Not a whole letter, just a line
parts.note: read typographically: a small stroke finishing off a printed character rather than a note sent by post

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone wrote only a brief note instead of a proper letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' and 'line' look like correspondence; they are a printed character and a pen stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In typography it is the short cross-stroke at the end of a character's main strokes, part of a letterform.

clue.text: Lady coming in incandescent after setback

indicators.note: a setback turns them round so they are read backwards
coming in says the letters sit within the word incandescent

explanation.surface: A woman arrives furious after a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after setback' turns ANDE, the run inside 'incandescent', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a woman's name, and in crosswords any female first name may be clued as a lady.

clue.text: An island? Solitary man doesn't need it

indicators.note: doesn't need means the word it is dropped from the end

parts.note: a hermit lives alone

explanation.surface: Asking whether a recluse living alone has no use for an island.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is one of the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Herm is a small car-free isle near Guernsey in the English Channel.

clue.text: It could be a firm assertion by the Spanish

parts.note: a vow is a solemn promise
EL is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Perhaps a company's declaration made by the Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It could be a' reads as a lead-in; it is the definition, since the letter A is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter A is an example of a vowel, as are E, I, O and U.

clue.text: Get in meat? It's not like meat

indicators.note: in places the word get within the word for meat

parts.note: veal is calf meat

explanation.surface: A question about putting meat on the shopping list, answered by something quite different.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetal means relating to plants, so it describes something of the vegetable rather than animal kind.

clue.text: Lion gets shot possibly in African country

indicators.note: gets means takes in, so the lion's letters hold the others

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of shot may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A lion is perhaps shot in an African land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lion' is the zodiac sign rather than a beast; 'possibly' scrambles 'shot' and 'gets' means the lion's letters take in the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountainous kingdom wholly surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Like hair that's propped up when falling apart!

definitions.text: Like hair that's propped up when falling apart!

parts.words: Like hair that's propped up when falling apart!
parts.note: read as a word for supported broken in two: the second half of that word describes locks of hair

explanation.surface: Hair that needs support because it is coming loose.
explanation.walkthrough: A word meaning propped up, as a wall is supported, falls apart after its first three letters, and what is left describes hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Having long locks, or arranged in tresses, describes hair worn long.

clue.text: Most expensive honey

explanation.surface: The priciest sweet spread, or a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means costly, so its superlative is costliest; it is also a loving form of address like darling.

clue.text: Vehicle in market reversing

indicators.note: reversing tells the solver to read the word for market backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A car backing up in a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails along city streets.

clue.text: Model or work in an office?

explanation.surface: Whether a model can do office work.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a model or typical example; to type is to use a keyboard, typical clerical work.

clue.text: Places one army officer goes up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soldier and a senior officer climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Loci is the plural of locus, Latin for a position or site.

clue.text: Abused queen died in meadow

indicators.note: in places the letter for died within the word for meadow

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogy

explanation.surface: A mistreated monarch dies in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus, in the form of a swan, seduced the queen of Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was the Spartan queen violated by Zeus disguised as a swan.

clue.text: Unadventurous types misrepresented as hot and steamy

indicators.note: misrepresented means presented wrongly, so the letters are given a false new order

explanation.surface: Something hot and steamy, depicted as such in error.
explanation.definitionFit: People who prefer to stay in rather than go out or travel are seen as unadventurous.

clue.text: On the church in days gone by

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A note about the church in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: Representative making call — agile or awkward?

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and ungainly, so the letters of the fodder tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether a phone call is nimble or clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegorical work uses characters and events to stand for ideas, so it is symbolic.
